data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew word 'Ail', meaning 'lion' or 'warrior'. In Christian tradition, the name Aileen is a feminine form of the masculine name Aidan, which means 'little fire'. Aileen is a name of strength and courage, reminding us of the lion of Judah and the brave warriors of the faith. The name Aileen carries the meaning “Little Lion” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Aileen usually hope their child will grow to embody little lion and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: עלין
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מקור השם איילן מעלין, שמשמעותו 'משורר', 'שורר' או 'פלא' (עברית: 'קסם'). מקורו בעברית עתיקה, והוא מופיע בכתבי ישראל הקדומים. בנוסף, 'עלין' יכול להתייחס לאדם שמצליח להשיג דברים גדולים, או לאדם שמביע את עצמיו באמצעות שירה. שם זה מאוזכר בפסוק: 'ישעיהו 13:6'.

in_greek.name: Αἰλίνη
in_greek.long_meaning: שם האיילן (Αἰλίνη) עם משמעות 'שורר' (Greek: 'ποίησις') או 'פלא' (Greek: 'θαῦμα') מקורו ביוונית. השם 'Αἰλίνη' (Ailine) הוא רבי-צורה של 'Αἰλίνε' (Ailine), שמשמעותו 'בת השורר' או 'בת הפלא'. 'Αἰλίνη' (Ailine) הופיע בפסוקים: 'Matthew 2:18', 'Matthew 2:24'.

They had a child, but Aileen was heartbroken when her husband was unable to provide her with the magical jewels she needed to maintain her youth and beauty. In her anger and despair, she cursed the child to be forever changed into a monster, known as the Selkie of Foulis. This myth originated from the Hebrides and dates back to the 16th century.

In medieval Christian tradition, Aileen was considered a variant of the name Alan or Aline, which was borne by several saints. Saint Aileen of Iona, also known as Saint Ailean, was a 6th-century Irish monk who is said to have founded a monastery on the Isle of Iona and is venerated as the patron saint of Iona. Saint Aileen of Cornwall, also known as Saint Elian or Saint Alian, was a 5th-century Welsh saint who is said to have been martyred during the Roman persecution of Christians.
